findings_qualitative.value: CO redshift agrees with low-ion absorption within ~40 km/s, disfavoring bulk-motion gas scenarios

evidence.quote: disfavors scenarios where the absorber is probing gas with a bulk motion with respect to the galaxy

claims.hypothesis: High-metallicity z~2 DLAs arise near massive gas-rich galaxies
claims.experiment: ALMA CO(3-2) search around the DLA sightline
claims.result: CO detected 3.5'' (30 kpc) away at the DLA redshift with M_mol ~1.4e11 Msun
claims.finding: Galaxy is associated with the DLA; consistent with massive-galaxy origin

evidence.quote: confirms the association between the molecular gas-rich galaxy and the high-metallicity absorber

claims.experiment: Compare Halpha SFR with TIR-based SFR

evidence.quote: Comparison of the two SFRs suggest that the galaxy is highly dust-obscured

claims.finding: Cold components contribute little HI but ~50% of metals

evidence.quote: the cold components in the DLA contribute little to the H I column density, yet contain roughly 50 % of the metals of the absorber

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Starburst-like alpha_CO~1 and r31~1 (mass lower by ~10) disfavored since the SFR is below typical starburst SFRs

evidence.quote: However, we disfavor this scenario, as even the dust-corrected SFR estimate is significantly below the median SFRs seen in starburst galaxies

limitations_admitted.value: L_TIR has large systematic uncertainty because beta and T_dust are unconstrained by a single continuum point

evidence.quote: This estimate has a large systematic uncertainty ($\sim$0.6 dex) because both $\beta$ and $\text{T}_{\text{dust}}$ are not constrained by the single dust continuum measurement.
